test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 09 May 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error’.

Our passage across the Arabian Sea/ was smooth as the most timid of/ navigators could desire.

options.text: Our passage across the Arabian Sea
was smooth as the most timid of

solution:
The erroneous part is: **was smooth as the most timid of**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ‘As’ is used to denote equality. It is used when a sentence contains **adjectives **in the positive and comparative forms.
 
• It is used in this manner: as ______ as. The blank should be an adjective.
 
 
• Example: She is** as good as**, if not better than her brother.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in the given question, "as...as" is being used in a slightly more complex way to compare the smoothness of the passage to the level of smoothness that the most timid of navigators could desire.
 
• This is a figurative comparison, expressing that the passage was extremely smooth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *Our passage across the Arabian Sea was **as **smooth as the most timid of navigators could desire.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• Remember, **NOT** all adjectives can be used in the structure "as + adjective + as".
 
• It's typically used with gradable adjectives — adjectives that can have different degrees or levels.
 
• For instance, words like 'happy', 'excited', 'sad', 'good', 'bad', 'smooth' etc., can be used, but non-gradable adjectives like 'dead', 'perfect', 'unique' typically are not used in this structure.
